August 18

9 But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain. 10 A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject; (Titus 3:9-10 KJV)

Paul is telling Titus not to argue over foolish questions, as it is not profitable. There are many questions that can be asked that are not because the person wants to know the truth, but may just want to argue. The Word of God should be explained to the person, but not argued over. If they want to argue about doctrine, works of the law, interpretation, etc., it is not something to be argued over. You will never make a person believe the Word by arguing them into believing, so it is unprofitable to do so.

If a person continues to want to argue over the Gospel or Word, you should correct them once or twice, but then if they just want to keep arguing, you should just reject them and not converse with them anymore. The Word of God is truth and is spirit (John 17:17), and many people cannot understand it as they try to read it with their minds and not their hearts. You must let the Holy Spirit (Comforter) help you understand Godâ€™s Word (John 14:26). Thank you Lord for the Comforter.
